A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GADGET framework and include readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–F. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification experiments on Airport, Citation, Social, and synthetic CSBM graphs, together with sensitivity, confidence, and runtime analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds an Airport experiment varying the FGW feature/structure weight α.

M1.justification: The FGW interpolation, low-rank OT solver, entropy-based confidence weighting, and self-training procedures remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2. The added edge- and graph-level definitions extend the theoretical treatment rather than document a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate node classification on the same Airport, Citation, Social, and CSBM domains, including attribute, degree, and homophily shifts. The broader theoretical task coverage is not accompanied by edge- or graph-level experiments.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain ERM, MMD, CORAL, AdaGCN, GRADE, and StruRW. FGW-Mixup and G-Mixup already participate in v1 Figure 9 and remain in v2 Figure 10; their newly supplied citations do not introduce new comparators.

E3.justification: v2 Figure 6 introduces an Airport sensitivity protocol evaluating α at 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1. The existing benchmark settings in Appendix D remain unchanged, including α=0.5, q=2, T=3, backbone configurations, and 1,000 training epochs.

E4.justification: Section 6.5 and Figure 6 add an analysis of feature/structure weighting, including feature-only and structure-only endpoints. The shift, step-count, rank, runtime, path-quality, and pseudo-label-confidence analyses otherwise already exist in v1, often in its appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over five runs. Shaded bands already appear in v1 sensitivity plots; v2 adds no distinct uncertainty-estimation procedure, seed information, confidence-interval definition, or significance testing.

E6.justification: The new α experiment reports lower Airport accuracy at the endpoints than at the best interior setting for each plotted method. Figure 2 and Table 1 retain the benchmark results, including average improvements of 6.77%, 3.58%, 3.43%, and 36.51% on Airport, Social, Citation, and CSBM, respectively.

T1.justification: v2 adds edge- and graph-level task definitions, aggregation/pooling assumptions, task-specific constants, and corresponding extensions of Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 with appendix proofs. It changes the stated Hölder exponent range from q≥1 to q>1 and introduces Theorem 4 and Appendix A.4 on low-rank approximation error.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly expands the error-bound contribution to node-, edge-, and graph-level tasks, and the introduction removes the node-only framing of the framework. This substantially broadens the claimed theoretical scope. The first graph-GDA claim, FGW-geodesic contribution, and headline 6.8% empirical improvement remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation that extremely large shifts can require enough adaptation steps for accumulated training error to outweigh the benefit. It also interprets the α experiment and explicitly identifies quadratic scalability as a limitation, proposing graph coarsening as future work. Mild/no-shift weaknesses were already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 adds a code-repository link absent from v1. Appendix D retains the data-generation instructions, model sizes, learning rate, training budget, software, and hardware disclosures; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: The background bibliography receives limited additions and removals, including adding PlanetAlign and newer Zeng et al. works and removing PageRank Bandits. Section 5 more explicitly describes the path-generation algorithm as adapted from Zeng et al. (2024c). The central positioning against graph DA and IID gradual adaptation remains.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: related work moves near the beginning, existing appendix analyses become dedicated main-text subsections, assumptions and proofs receive additional subdivisions, and the algorithm and experimental appendices exchange order. Much prose is retained, but the narrative structure changes extensively.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different title-page and journal layout, replaces embedding panels in Figures 1 and 3, and extensively rearranges analysis displays. v1 appendix Figures 5, 7, and 8 become main-text Figures 4 and 5, with the hyperparameter plots merged; a new α plot is added. Benchmark plots and table contents largely remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The α experiment, code-access information, and clearer failure/scalability discussion provide limited gains in validation and reproducibility. The substantial theoretical expansion has qualifications: the new graph-level derivation in Appendix A.1 drops a q-th power, and Appendix A.4 assumes an unexplained identity alignment between exact and rank-r graphs. These issues limit the theoretical gain; with the established benchmark evidence unchanged, the supported overall improvement is modest.
